items: New draft 1D (shown first): 1C, plus your ending with the nan.
Line 3's wine fridge is now a blank, with ten funnier hardships to pick from in 1D's notes (two nod at the 2009 expenses scandal: the duck house and the moat).
Her line 'Poor bastard...' is in verbatim.
Keep 'Or keep your £3. You're going to need it.' before the nan, or cut it (the nan is now the button)?
The name: Crispin clashes with a real ex-MP (Crispin Blunt). Pick another and I'll check it.

replies.1-1C-L3: Answered in draft 1D: the wine fridge is now a blank with ten options (duck house, last moat, one-towel towel rail, pony sharing a paddock, part-time butler, second home's second home, last thousand bottles, one-week ski trip, swans without scarves, or yours). My pick: the duck house or the moat, because the real 2009 expenses claims make them land harder with the reader.

kai_round1.1-1C-L3: we need something else other than second wine frige that is funny thanks
kai_round1.chat: 1c is fine... after the advert, the camera could pan to a freezing working class nan, she goes to the door to pick up junk mail, one of them is a advert for the politician looking sadder, then her saying "poor bastard..."
